html:
The main railway of New Zealand's North Island, joining the capital Wellington to Auckland, the largest city. Work on the hard central section began in 1885 and the line was finished in 1908. It runs 682 km.

The two ends had been built out from the cities, but the middle crossed the King Country, land held by Māori of the King Movement who had shut it to settlers after the New Zealand Wars. In 1885 their leaders agreed to let the railway through. Engineers then had to cross the rugged volcanic plateau around Mount Ruapehu. They built tall steel viaducts over deep gorges and the Raurimu Spiral, a loop of track with tunnels and horseshoe curves that climbs a steep slope.

The last spike was driven in November 1908 by the prime minister Joseph Ward. The line opened the centre of the island to farming and settlement. On Christmas Eve 1953 a volcanic mudflow from Ruapehu swept away a bridge at Tangiwai, and a train fell into the river, killing 151 people, New Zealand's worst rail disaster. See New Zealand and Māori.
